title: Rust graph authority and per-package API contracts
objective: Record the owner's decision that reusable graph structures and calculations are authoritative in Rust while callers own presentation enrichment, and require generated public-API baselines plus behavioral contract tests for consumed packages.
validations: repository owner explicitly required Rust authority for graph structures and calculations on 2026-07-29
control-plane audit passed with zero model calls and zero side effects
Graph IR candidate generation and freshness check passed with 26 nodes and 20 edges
manual authority, dependency-direction, vendor-isolation, and API-contract review passed
risks: A manually maintained universal IDL would duplicate native public APIs and drift.
Exposing petgraph, nalgebra, X6, or other vendor types would make Grafting contracts depend on replaceable implementations.
API signature snapshots cannot prove behavior; consumed packages also require behavioral contract tests.
